data.title: Axonius parser fixes: finish, review and commit (CA-67590)
data.goal: Finish the Axonius parser in cymulate-integration-parsers (worktree /Users/user/Dev/_axonius-dev/cymulate-integration-parsers, branch feat/ca-67590-axonius-parser from origin/master c171783). The candidate is uncommitted in that worktree: task 2026-09-23_1034-axonius-yaml-bundle built it as W2, then fixed it as W4 (finding de-duplication removed because exposure analytics merges duplicates, _first_data continues to later adapters, UTF-8 BOM stripped); W4 was verified (VOUT9, E30 full suite 365 passed, E31 mutations and end-to-end exposure-analytics check) but not code-reviewed, and was cancelled Stale by the operator (D12). This task establishes the candidate's identity, gives it an independent code review and any repair it needs, runs the suite host-side through ailedger verification run, and hands it to the operator for commit and push review. The bundle (magic-integration 422f83a, pushed) is out of scope; the other repositories are read-only.

lesson.statement: rules[].value reaches Postgres as native JSON, so Exposure Analytics can read toggle and slider values.
lesson.outcome: The verify query was not run. Definitions now travel through a new NDJSON staging codec and back through RehydrateDefinitions -- a changed serialization path on the exact field that broke before. Previously REFUTED as L-5de41efb.
lesson.verify: psql -c "select distinct jsonb_typeof(value) from cybi.security_policy_rule" -- 'string' reproduces the defect, 'object' is correct
lesson.doNot: Do not treat a successful write as proof the payload is consumable; assert jsonb_typeof on nested values after changing a serialization path.

lesson.statement: An 89-character combined id is safe in parser output columns that have only ever carried 32-character AIDs.
lesson.outcome: No consumer downstream of the parser was probed. asset_match_key was scoped out of the task, so the join most likely to notice was deliberately not examined.
lesson.doNot: do not assume a widened identity column lands downstream without checking the match key that consumes it

lesson.statement: The S3 Tenable samples are enough to sanity-check that a second vendor shape fits the same normalizer with no code change.
lesson.outcome: The check was dropped and the recording the decision required was never made: no tenable reference exists anywhere in src/, tests/ or execution_notes.md. Vendor-agnosticism rests on token absence plus exactly one vendor actually run.
lesson.verify: grep -ril tenable /Users/user/Dev/Uri/localprojects/adapter-data-normalizer/src /Users/user/Dev/Uri/localprojects/adapter-data-normalizer/tests || echo 'no tenable reference — claim still unexercised'
lesson.doNot: do not accept a vendor-agnosticism claim proven against one vendor and a grep for vendor tokens

lesson.statement: A vendor nested value reaches Postgres as native JSON rather than a double-encoded string in every column that carries one.
lesson.outcome: Proven only for additional_fields (jsonb_typeof='object' on 294/294 asset rows). The column the original lesson concerned is plain text here and was never exercised.
lesson.doNot: do not generalise a jsonb round-trip proof to a text column carrying JSON

lesson.statement: A widened identity value reaching parser output columns lands correctly in the downstream match key that consumes it.
lesson.outcome: No identity was widened in this task and no EA code was executed. The downstream match key was read, never run.
lesson.verify: none — citation is not mechanically checkable
lesson.doNot: do not assume a widened identity column lands downstream without running the match key that consumes it

lesson.statement: Aligning a new normalizer to the production parser column by column captures every material divergence from it.
lesson.outcome: Column-by-column alignment omits the default-value class entirely, which was the largest divergence by far. Measured on 298 real Falcon asset rows: os_type 248 null where production emits other, os_version 248 null vs other, os_build 248 null vs empty string, fqdn 286 null vs empty string - 83 to 96 percent of rows, against a divergence of 1 row that was documented at length.
citations: crowdstrikeAssets.py:66 default_value=Other, lowercased at base_parser.py:231ff; measured over out rows (verifier, 2026-09-06) (verifier, 2026-09-06)
lesson.doNot: do not treat a source-path comparison as a mapping comparison - compare defaults and post-processing too

lesson.statement: A vendor nested value reaches Postgres as native JSON rather than a double-encoded string.
lesson.outcome: Unobserved here - no Postgres write is in scope - but production double-encodes 6 of 54 additional_fields members via F.to_json: cvss_vector, vpr, port, scan, vpr_v2 and cvss_temporal_vector are JSON strings inside the JSON. This normalizer keeps them native, so the two differ at that boundary.
lesson.doNot: do not assume the two pipelines agree on nested-value encoding without comparing a written column

lesson.statement: Guess backend field names for the Axonius native Business Unit, Asset Criticality, Device Ownership and Axonius Risk Score fields and put them in fields[]
lesson.outcome: No public or community source gives their backend names (NC4, NC5, NC6, NC8); a guessed name returns nothing and reads as a real mapping. They stay tenant checks; the adapter fields already arrive inside specific_data. Recorded by the operator for axonius-enrichment-fields (RR11), whose role lacks RecordAlternative.
lesson.verify: none — the vendor backend names are behind a gated reference; nothing in a repository can re-establish them
lesson.doNot: put a guessed vendor backend field name into a bundle fields list or a parser mapping, or promote a value a mock invented; leave it null and list it as a tenant check

lesson.statement: De-duplicate CVE findings per (asset_id, cve_id) inside the Axonius parser hook (D8 item 2, D9 items 2 and 3)
lesson.outcome: Exposure analytics already merges duplicate (asset, CVE) rows with its own rule (worst severity, active status wins, earliest/latest seen), and no active sibling parser de-duplicates findings (E28); a second rule in the parser disagreed with EA's on status (PGC21). Operator, 2026-09-23: remove it.
lesson.doNot: de-duplicate CVE findings in a parser; exposure analytics create-entities-tp merges duplicate asset/CVE rows itself (worst severity, active status, earliest and latest seen), and no active parser de-duplicates findings

lesson.statement: The W2 parser drops per-CVE first_seen and last_seen: for CVE-2024-10004 in findings_rich.json (first_fetch_time 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, last_fetch_time 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z), the Spark output has first_seen and last_seen null, although axonius_yaml_hook.py:148 passes both through.

artifact.content:
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "taskId": "2026-09-23_2014-axonius-parser-fixes",
  "claimSetHash": "628cf0d2fdd34dce711ee968804abcd94ed260956c930eb6125bcb07629de6fd",
  "assessments": [
    {
      "claimId": "C1",
      "domain": "internal"
    },
    {
      "claimId": "C2",
      "domain": "internal"
    }
  ],
  "report": "# Internal Recon

## Durable sources read
- `cymulate-integration-parsers/CLAUDE.md:1-110` — YAML registration, BaseParser shaping, fixture discovery, wheel packaging and Spark test conventions. The task's K1/K2 constraints narrow execution further.
- Prior task `2026-09-23_1034-axonius-yaml-bundle/review/verifier-9.md` (VOUT9) and `review/code-reviewer-7.md` (CR7-W2) — W4 passed verification after removing parser-side finding de-duplication, changing `_first_data`, and stripping a UTF-8 BOM; W4 itself did not receive the subsequent independent code review. This task's C1/E1 and C2/E2 establish candidate identity and the assurance gap.
- Recalled lessons `ALT3`, `ALT4`, `C15` from the prior task — treated as prior evidence to check against current code and the downstream consumer, not as new vendor facts.

## Files in scope
- `libs/packages/parsers/yaml_engine/specs/axonius-assets-findings.yaml:1-25` — parser key, findings-lane metadata and bespoke process hook; W1 review and conditional repair.
- `libs/packages/parsers/axonius/__init__.py:1` — parser package marker; W1 review.
- `libs/packages/parsers/axonius/axonius_yaml_hook.py:16-223` — device/CVE normalization, pre-shaping schemas, Spark asset/finding linkage; W1 review and conditional repair.
- `tests/test_axonius_assets_findings.py:1-216` — focused fixture, fallback, BOM, timestamp and duplicate-CVE checks; W1 review and conditional repair.
- `test_files/axonius/assets_and_findings/findings.json` and `findings_rich.json` — bundle-derived NDJSON inputs; W1 review and conditional repair only if a defect requires it.
- `test_files/axonius/assets_and_findings/findings.expected_assets.json`, `findings.expected_findings.json`, `findings_rich.expected_assets.json`, `findings_rich.expected_findings.json` — golden parser outputs; W1 review and conditional repair only if a defect requires it.

## Patterns to mirror
- Spec registration → `libs/packages/parsers/__init__.py:26-54` — packaged YAML specs register parser factories; no central registry edit is needed.
- Bespoke hook lifecycle → `libs/packages/parsers/yaml_engine/yaml_parser.py:239-244` and `:319-342` — `process_hook` owns loading and returns pre-shaping frames, then ordinary post-processing applies because the Axonius spec sets `skip_post_shaping: false`.
- Shared output shaping → `libs/packages/parsers/common/base_parser.py:220-320,561-607` — filters invalid asset identities, normalizes enums, explodes CVEs, creates source rows and lowercases output. Review must judge final output, including defaults and post-processing, not only hook tuples.
- One findings lane and stamped linkage → `libs/packages/parsers/yaml_engine/specs/armis-assets-findings.yaml:24-48,107-110` and `yaml_parser.py:453-469` — sibling parser uses a single findings lane and a shared row asset ID. Axonius hook stamps `_row_asset_id` on the pair frame and selects it into both lanes (`axonius_yaml_hook.py:201-223`).
- Golden harness → `tests/test_run_parsers.py:1-15,137-154` — spec fixtures exercise parser registration and Spark output; current Axonius focused test uses a real Spark fixture for duplicate rows (`tests/test_axonius_assets_findings.py:196-216`).

## Downstream acceptance and merge
- Exposure Analytics accepts only parser assets with valid asset type and OS enum, then inserts enriched assets (`cymulate-exposure-analytics/apps/create-entities-tp/src/app/create-entities-third-party/repositories/parsed-data.repository.ts:352-423`). It accepts exposures with valid type, status and severity, and with an enriched parent asset (`:524-552`). This makes the BaseParser post-shaping boundary material.
- Exposure Analytics always merges same `(asset_id, cve_id)` findings: oldest `first_seen`, newest `last_seen`, worst severity, and active status before resolved (`parsed-data.repository.ts:553-591`). It then requires a non-rejected `cve_details` match (`:593-599`). The parser should emit each adapter row and retain the evidence EA merges; the current hook does so (`axonius_yaml_hook.py:147-167,219-223`). This re-establishes the local part of recalled `ALT4` without changing EA.
- Recalled `ALT3`: the hook reads adapter `specific_data[].data` for supported enrichment names (`axonius_yaml_hook.py:98-99,122-139`) and leaves native risk score null (`:140-146`); the spec says the native backend name remains a tenant check (`axonius-assets-findings.yaml:22-25`). Do not infer vendor native field names from mock data.
- Recalled `C15`: the current rich fixture has per-CVE fetch times; the hook parses them into `TimestampType` fields (`axonius_yaml_hook.py:50-64,163-197`), focused tests assert them (`tests/test_axonius_assets_findings.py:60-64,76-92`), and `findings_rich.expected_findings.json` contains non-null first/last seen for `cve-2024-10004`. The prior W2 loss is not present in this candidate's golden output. A fresh assurance pass still checks these final fields.

## Shared surface to freeze
- W1 is one work item; no sibling worker interface needs freezing. Its review target is the exact ten-file candidate identified by C1/E1. Any repair changes the candidate identity and requires fresh verification and independent review of the changed bytes.
- `ailedger.verification.json` is the operator's untracked host verification profile and is excluded from the candidate and commits (K1).

## Disjoint sets available
- None for the assigned W1 scope: the spec selects the hook; the tests and snapshots assert that hook's final output through BaseParser. Review and a possible narrow repair concern one candidate and one assurance boundary. No implementation is authorized in this recon run.

## Landmines
- A hook-side duplicate winner can mask an active CVE state or discard date/severity evidence that EA's canonical merge uses (`parsed-data.repository.ts:553-591`; recalled `ALT4`).
- A thin fixture can pass while final per-CVE seen times are null; the rich fixture and golden output must remain in assurance (`tests/test_axonius_assets_findings.py:40-73`; recalled `C15`).
- `_first_data` must continue past whitespace and non-string adapter values (`axonius_yaml_hook.py:67-78`; `tests/test_axonius_assets_findings.py:153-161`).
- The hook reads text lines as JSON and fails loudly on malformed objects; BOM removal is a narrow tolerance (`axonius_yaml_hook.py:96-99,201-215`; `tests/test_axonius_assets_findings.py:164-170`).
- Governed runs cannot run Spark or Docker (K2). The operator's host-side verification profile is required for the full suite; prior E30 is historical evidence for the unchanged candidate, not a substitute if repair changes bytes.
"
}

artifact.title: Axonius parser candidate completion contract
artifact.content:
Role:
You are a Python/PySpark parser engineer completing independent assurance for an existing Axonius parser candidate.

Goal:
Confirm the ten-file uncommitted Axonius parser candidate in `cymulate-integration-parsers`, obtain an independent review of its current bytes, repair only an on-our-side silent data defect if found, run the operator's host-side parser suite, and hand the assured candidate to the operator for commit and push review.

Context:
- Worktree: `/Users/user/Dev/_axonius-dev/cymulate-integration-parsers`, branch `feat/ca-67590-axonius-parser`, base `c17178329284c254947b3b811e10c4d45ff78684`.
- Prior task `2026-09-23_1034-axonius-yaml-bundle` produced W4. Its VOUT9, E30 and E31 verified candidate `c8faa615669a95fb3e538378673781ccef41b9fede1ac67bfed349dab64f5ed5`; W4 was cancelled before its independent code review. Current C1/E1 and C2/E2 establish identity and that gap.
- `research/internal-recon.md` and filed `IR1` map the parser, sibling conventions, Exposure Analytics acceptance/merge behavior, and recalled `ALT3`, `ALT4`, `C15`.

Constraints:

* Product writes are limited to `libs/packages/parsers/yaml_engine/specs/axonius-assets-findings.yaml`, `libs/packages/parsers/axonius/`, `test_files/axonius/assets_and_findings/`, and `tests/test_axonius_assets_findings.py` in the named worktree.
* The untracked root `ailedger.verification.json` is the operator's profile. Exclude it from the candidate and any commit.
* `cymulate-magic-integration`, `cymulate-integration-adapters`, `yaml-adapter-engine`, and `cymulate-exposure-analytics` are read-only. Do not change the bundle, shared parser engine, or downstream merge rules.
* Governed runs may not start Spark or Docker. The operator runs the full parser suite host-side through `ailedger verification run --profile parser-suite`. A governed run may use only K2's focused pytest command if runnable.
* Keep every adapter's CVE row for Exposure Analytics to merge; do not add a parser-side deduplication rule. Do not guess tenant-only Axonius native backend names. Keep rich-fixture per-CVE timestamp coverage.
* Commit and push belong to the operator. Start every `ailedger` invocation with `/Users/user/.dotnet/tools/ailedger` and use the task root supplied in the manifest.

Success Criteria:

* The work item records the complete ten-file candidate identity and compares it with C1/E1 and the prior W4 candidate; no unrelated or operator-owned file is included.
* A fresh independent verifier pass covers the frozen candidate, followed by a fresh isolated paired code review of the same bytes. Findings are evaluated and disposed; any on-our-side silent data defect is repaired within the four allowed paths and receives fresh assurance.
* Final parser output preserves one asset per input device and all adapter CVE rows linked to it, usable fallback values, BOM handling, and non-null per-CVE seen times when supplied; final enum and CVE fields remain consumable by Exposure Analytics. The rich fixture and tests supply direct checks.
* The operator's host-side `parser-suite` verification run passes against the final candidate. If bytes change after it, the suite and assurance are repeated on the changed candidate.
* The final hand-off gives the operator exact candidate files and digest, test/assurance results, any accepted risks or tenant checks, and the commit/push review boundary. No commit or push occurs in this task run.

Execution Rules:

* Do not assume missing data; cite repository code, prior task records, and current run evidence.
* Respect constraints strictly.
* Review the original candidate before changing code. Repair only a demonstrated on-our-side defect that silently loses or distorts data or breaks a contract criterion; route any scope change to the operator.
* Keep verifier and code reviewer separate, with the reviewer receiving only the kernel's neutral minimal context. Compare candidate bytes before and after each assurance pass.

Output Format:
- `research/internal-recon.md` and `research/internal-recon.json` hold the filed recon.
- `orchestration_plan.md` holds the task plan and one W1 work-item brief.
- W1 writes `execution_notes.md`; the verifier and reviewer write separate numbered files under `review/` and file their governed artifacts.
- The operator receives a concise commit-review hand-off naming the candidate digest, exact paths, checks, findings and unresolved tenant checks.

Stop Conditions:

* When the goal is achieved.
* When required data is missing and would change implementation or assurance.
* When a repair needs a file outside K1, changes a read-only repository, or would require bypassing independent verification.
